fields.name: timestamp
fields.description: Normalized event timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC format
fields.justification: Enables chronological sorting and time-range queries across all sources in 3x02 detections and 3x03 triage

source_mapping.windows_json: timestamp_raw parsed as ISO 8601 and converted explicitly to UTC using astimezone(timezone.utc)
source_mapping.linux_text: auth.log/syslog: 'Mon DD HH:MM:SS' parsed with year inferred as 2026 and timezone.utc assigned; audit.log: epoch from msg=audit(EPOCH:COUNTER) converted with datetime.fromtimestamp(epoch, tz=timezone.utc)
source_mapping.network_csv: epoch seconds in timestamp column converted with datetime.fromtimestamp(float(timestamp), tz=timezone.utc) and formatted as ISO 8601 UTC
source_mapping.network_json: suricata_eve.json: timestamp parsed as ISO 8601 with timezone and converted using astimezone(timezone.utc); pcap_summary.json: start_time parsed with strptime('%m/%d/%Y %I:%M:%S %p'), timezone.utc assigned, then formatted as ISO 8601 UTC

fields.name: hostname
fields.description: Hostname of the system that generated the event, or null for network-only sources
fields.justification: Allows analysts to filter events by host and correlate activity across sources during triage

source_mapping.windows_json: hostname field from the NDJSON record
source_mapping.linux_text: auth.log/syslog: token after timestamp in syslog header; audit.log: hostname key from parsed audit fields when present

fields.name: source_type
fields.description: Origin telemetry type of the event: windows_json, linux_text, firewall, suricata, or pcap_flow
fields.justification: Lets downstream queries filter consistently by telemetry source without inspecting vendor-specific fields

source_mapping.windows_json: constant: windows_json
source_mapping.linux_text: constant: linux_text
source_mapping.network_json: derived from input file identity: suricata_eve.json -> suricata; pcap_summary.json -> pcap_flow

fields.name: event_category
fields.description: High-level category such as authentication, process, file, network, network_alert, network_flow, audit, powershell, or service
fields.justification: Needed by 3x02 detection rules and 3x03 triage filters to group events independently of source vendor

source_mapping.windows_json: Security event IDs 4624, 4625, 4634, and 4648 -> authentication; 4720 and 4726 -> authentication; Sysmon event ID 1 -> process, 3 -> network, 11 -> file; PowerShell event ID 4104 -> powershell
source_mapping.linux_text: audit_type USER_AUTH, USER_LOGIN, USER_ACCT, or CRED_ACQ -> authentication; SYSCALL -> process; SERVICE_START or SERVICE_STOP -> service; PATH or AVC -> audit; program sshd, su, or login -> authentication; sudo -> process; kernel or UFW -> network; otherwise audit

fields.name: severity
fields.description: Normalized severity level: info, low, medium, high, or critical
fields.justification: Enables prioritization of alerts in 3x03 triage and severity-based filtering in 3x02

source_mapping.windows_json: event ID mapping: 4625 -> medium; 4720 -> high; 7045 -> high; 4698 -> high; 4624 -> info; 4634 -> info; Sysmon process creation -> info unless explicitly classified otherwise
source_mapping.linux_text: audit res=failed -> medium; res=success -> info; auth message containing 'Failed password' -> medium; 'Accepted password' or 'session opened' -> info; sudo -> low
source_mapping.network_csv: action BLOCK -> low; action ALLOW -> info
source_mapping.network_json: suricata alert.severity 1 -> high, 2 -> medium, 3 -> low; pcap_summary.json -> info

fields.name: user
fields.description: Username associated with the event, or null when no user identity is available
fields.justification: Supports correlation of account activity across systems and investigation of authentication or lateral movement

source_mapping.windows_json: event_data.TargetUserName for Security events; event_data.User for Sysmon when available
source_mapping.linux_text: user field parsed from auth.log/syslog or acct field parsed from audit.log

fields.name: process_name
fields.description: Name or executable path of the process associated with the event, or null when not applicable
fields.justification: Enables process-based detection rules and behavioral investigation in 3x02 and 3x03

source_mapping.windows_json: event_data.Image or event_data.ProcessName when present
source_mapping.linux_text: program from syslog header or comm field from audit.log

fields.name: src_ip
fields.description: Source IP address associated with the event, or null when unavailable
fields.justification: Supports network correlation, source attribution, lateral movement analysis, and zone enrichment

source_mapping.windows_json: event_data.IpAddress for applicable Security events or event_data.SourceIp for Sysmon Event ID 3
source_mapping.linux_text: addr or src field from parsed_fields when present

fields.name: dst_ip
fields.description: Destination IP address associated with the event, or null when unavailable
fields.justification: Supports destination correlation, network investigation, exfiltration detection, and zone enrichment

source_mapping.windows_json: event_data.DestinationIp for Sysmon Event ID 3 or other events where available
source_mapping.linux_text: dst field from parsed_fields when present

fields.name: raw_message
fields.description: Original raw log message or serialized source record retained before normalization
fields.justification: Preserves forensic traceability to source evidence and allows analysts to inspect information not represented by normalized fields

source_mapping.windows_json: raw_message field from the intermediate Windows record
source_mapping.linux_text: full original line from auth.log, audit.log, or syslog
source_mapping.network_csv: original firewall CSV row reconstructed using the original column order
source_mapping.network_json: original JSON record serialized without dropping source fields

fields.name: event_id
fields.description: Windows Event ID associated with the event, or null for sources without a Windows Event ID
fields.justification: Enables Windows-specific detection logic based on well-known Security, Sysmon, and PowerShell Event IDs

source_mapping.windows_json: event_id field
source_mapping.linux_text: null

fields.name: source_origin
fields.description: Provenance tag identifying evidence_pack or student_telemetry as the record origin
fields.justification: Preserves provenance so analysts can distinguish supplied evidence from student-generated telemetry

source_mapping.windows_json: source_origin from intermediate record
source_mapping.linux_text: source_origin from intermediate record

fields.name: source_channel
fields.description: Windows event channel such as Security, Sysmon Operational, or PowerShell Operational
fields.justification: Allows Windows detections and analyst queries to distinguish logging subsystems

source_mapping.windows_json: channel field
source_mapping.linux_text: null

fields.name: source_provider
fields.description: Windows event provider responsible for generating the event
fields.justification: Allows detections to distinguish providers that may reuse similar event identifiers or fields

source_mapping.windows_json: provider field
source_mapping.linux_text: null

fields.name: pid
fields.description: Process identifier associated with the event, or null when no process context exists
fields.justification: Supports process correlation and reconstruction of activity involving the same running process

source_mapping.windows_json: event_data.ProcessId or event_data.Pid converted to integer when present
source_mapping.linux_text: pid from syslog header or pid key from audit.log converted to integer

fields.name: src_port
fields.description: Source port associated with the network event, or null when unavailable
fields.justification: Supports connection-level correlation and identification of network sessions

source_mapping.windows_json: event_data.SourcePort or event_data.IpPort converted to integer when present
source_mapping.linux_text: src_port or sport from parsed_fields when present

fields.name: dst_port
fields.description: Destination port associated with the network event, or null when unavailable
fields.justification: Supports service identification and correlation of traffic to destination applications

source_mapping.windows_json: event_data.DestinationPort converted to integer when present
source_mapping.linux_text: dst_port or dport from parsed_fields when present

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: Network protocol such as TCP, UDP, ICMP, DNS, HTTP, or TLS when available
fields.justification: Allows protocol-based filtering and correlation during network detection and triage

source_mapping.windows_json: event_data.Protocol normalized to uppercase when present
source_mapping.linux_text: proto or protocol from parsed_fields when present
source_mapping.network_json: suricata_eve.json: app_proto when present otherwise proto; pcap_summary.json: protocol

fields.name: action
fields.description: Outcome or enforcement action such as ALLOW, BLOCK, success, failed, or null
fields.justification: Allows analysts to distinguish permitted, blocked, successful, and failed activity during investigation

source_mapping.windows_json: null
source_mapping.linux_text: audit.log res field normalized to success or failed; auth.log Accepted -> success and Failed -> failed
source_mapping.network_csv: action column normalized to ALLOW or BLOCK
source_mapping.network_json: suricata_eve.json: alert.action when present; pcap_summary.json: null

fields.name: signature
fields.description: IDS or IPS alert signature associated with the event, or null
fields.justification: Supports Suricata alert correlation, signature-based investigation, and threat identification

source_mapping.windows_json: null
source_mapping.linux_text: null

fields.name: bytes_in
fields.description: Number of bytes received or associated with the inbound side of a connection when available
fields.justification: Supports traffic-volume analysis and identification of unusual data transfers

source_mapping.windows_json: null
source_mapping.linux_text: null
source_mapping.network_json: suricata_eve.json: flow.bytes_toclient when available; pcap_summary.json: bytes_total when only a total byte count exists

fields.name: bytes_out
fields.description: Number of bytes sent or associated with the outbound side of a connection when available
fields.justification: Supports detection and investigation of unusually large outbound transfers and possible exfiltration

source_mapping.windows_json: null
source_mapping.linux_text: null
source_mapping.network_json: suricata_eve.json: flow.bytes_toserver when available; pcap_summary.json: null

fields.name: event_data
fields.description: Structured source-specific payload retained alongside normalized fields
fields.justification: Preserves vendor-specific evidence needed for deep investigation without requiring the original source to be reparsed

source_mapping.windows_json: event_data object
source_mapping.linux_text: parsed_fields object
source_mapping.network_csv: object containing all original CSV columns and values
source_mapping.network_json: original structured JSON fields retained as an object

fields.name: record_id
fields.description: Deterministic SHA-256 identifier calculated from the canonical normalized record before record_id is added
fields.justification: Provides a stable identifier for referencing and correlating records without recursively hashing the record_id field itself

source_mapping.windows_json: derived after normalization as SHA-256 of json.dumps(record_without_record_id, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')) encoded as UTF-8
source_mapping.linux_text: derived after normalization as SHA-256 of json.dumps(record_without_record_id, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')) encoded as UTF-8
source_mapping.network_csv: derived after normalization as SHA-256 of json.dumps(record_without_record_id, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')) encoded as UTF-8
source_mapping.network_json: derived after normalization as SHA-256 of json.dumps(record_without_record_id, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')) encoded as UTF-8
